reason: Both conversations correctly landed on the dryer heater element or its thermal cut-out and sensibly escalated to an engineer, and neither asked the key question about the interrupted drying cycle or requested the full model number for parts. Conversation 1 was inefficient and repetitive, pushing the pump (drain) filter three times as an 'airflow' check even after the customer said she hadn't done it, offering a dubious 'sensor never triggers heat' theory, and giving one turn with no actionable step at all; its only advantage was confirming the programme wasn't a cool/eco setting. Conversation 2 told her to unplug before checking, got the filter and condenser actually cleaned, proposed a short test run as a clear decision point, and explained plainly what the engineer would replace and why it isn't a DIY job, so it moved the homeowner further with less friction.
